q: Which pairing of a COSO component with an example is accurate?
o: Control activities and audit committee oversight of reporting
Risk assessment and segregation of duties over cash receipts
Monitoring and internal audit evaluation of controls
Information and communication and the entity code of conduct
why: Ongoing and separate evaluations such as internal audit reviews are monitoring; audit committee oversight and the code of conduct sit in the control environment and segregation of duties is a control activity.

q: A walkthrough is performed primarily in order to:
o: Confirm the flow and evaluate design and implementation
Conclude on operating effectiveness across the whole period
Provide a statistically valid sample of the control operations
Discharge the SA 330 requirement for tests of controls
why: A walkthrough of one or a few transactions establishes understanding, design and implementation; a single instance cannot support an operating effectiveness conclusion or form a valid sample.

q: A control is well designed but the person performing it has no authority to enforce the follow up action. In an IFC evaluation this is best classified as:
o: A design deficiency, since the objective is not met as designed
An operating effectiveness deficiency and nothing further
Not a deficiency while the control sits in the process narrative
A compensating control matter needing no separate evaluation
why: A design deficiency exists where a control is missing or is not designed such that the objective is met even when operated as intended, which covers a performer lacking the necessary authority or competence.

q: Which best distinguishes a significant deficiency from a material weakness in IFC reporting?
o: A significant deficiency is a gap; a weakness is an actual error
A significant deficiency is reported; a weakness goes to management
A material weakness can arise only in listed public companies
A material weakness means material misstatement may go undetected
why: The distinction is severity measured by likelihood and magnitude of potential misstatement, not by whether an error occurred; a material weakness drives an adverse IFC opinion.

q: Reporting on internal financial controls under section 143 3 i of the Companies Act 2013 is NOT required for:
o: A listed public company of any size or turnover level
A public company with paid up share capital of 100 crore
An unlisted public company having bank borrowings of 60 crore
A private company meeting the notified exemption conditions
why: The exemption notification relieves certain private companies including one person and small companies and those within turnover and borrowing limits; all public companies remain covered.

q: Which of the following is a general IT control rather than an application control?
o: A three way match of purchase order, goods receipt and invoice
Restricted privileged database access with periodic review
A system edit check rejecting negative quantities on entry
Automatic sequential numbering of outgoing sales invoices
why: ITGCs cover access to programs and data, program change, development and computer operations; matching logic, edit checks and sequencing are application controls inside a business process.

q: ITGCs over program change management are found to be ineffective. For an automated three way match control this means:
o: The automated control still holds since a walkthrough passed
ITGC failures touch user access only, never processing logic
Reliance fails as the logic may have changed in the period
An adverse internal financial controls opinion follows at once
why: Automated controls depend on ITGCs for consistent operation across the period, so a change management failure means point in time testing may not represent the full period; severity still needs separate evaluation.

q: Which combination of duties held by one person creates the highest risk of undetected misappropriation of cash?
o: Recording sales invoices and preparing the receivables ageing list
Approving purchase orders and preparing the annual budget
Preparing bank reconciliations and filing statutory returns
Receiving cheques, posting receipts and authorising write offs
why: Custody of receipts combined with recording and write off authority allows lapping to be concealed by writing off the shortfall; the other pairings do not combine asset custody with the ability to hide a loss.

q: The extent of testing of a manual control that operates daily is influenced most by:
o: The absolute materiality of the related account balance
Frequency of operation, deviation rates and assurance sought
The number of employees working in the accounting department
The monetary value of the largest transaction processed
why: Attribute sampling for controls is driven by frequency and deviation rates and the assurance sought; monetary value drives substantive sampling rather than tests of controls.

q: One deviation is found in forty tested instances of an authorisation control. The most appropriate initial response is to:
o: Conclude the control is ineffective and abandon reliance now
Extend the sample by exactly forty further items in each case
Accept it since one in forty is within a normal tolerable rate
Investigate the cause and judge whether it is systematic
why: SA 530 requires investigation of the nature and cause of every deviation and consideration of its effect; neither automatic rejection nor mechanical extension nor dismissal is appropriate first.

q: Which statement about the auditor responsibility under section 143 3 i is most accurate?
o: The auditor designs and implements the internal controls
The conclusion is expressed as limited negative assurance
The auditor opines on adequacy and operating effectiveness
The conclusion covers all operational and compliance controls
why: Clause i requires a reasonable assurance opinion on adequacy and operating effectiveness with reference to the financial statements; establishing and maintaining controls remains a management and board responsibility.

q: Entity level controls that are sufficiently precise may:
o: Replace all transaction level control testing in the audit
Be evaluated for design only and never for effectiveness
Be ignored wherever process level controls are documented
Reduce but not always eliminate transaction level testing
why: A highly precise management review can reduce process level testing, but most entity level controls are indirect and support the environment rather than addressing specific assertions.

q: The essential difference between a test of controls and a test of details is that:
o: Controls testing evidences operation; details evidence amounts
A test of controls always uses a larger sample than a test of details
A test of details can be performed only at the year end date
A test of controls is mandated by statute for all companies
why: Tests of controls target the operation of the control and are evaluated by deviation rates, whereas tests of details target recorded amounts and are evaluated in monetary terms.

o: Testing two different controls from a single document sample
Testing the same control at interim and again at the year end date
One sample evidences control operation and monetary accuracy
Two auditors independently reperform the identical procedure
why: A dual purpose test combines a test of controls with a test of details on the same items, though the auditor must confirm the sample size satisfies both attribute and monetary objectives.

q: Which would most likely constitute a material weakness in IFC for a manufacturing company?
o: A two day delay in preparing one monthly bank reconciliation file
Absence of a written petty cash policy below a small limit
Occasional missing second signature on low value requisitions
An ineffective revenue control allowing material error to pass
why: Material weakness turns on a reasonable possibility that material misstatement is not prevented or detected, which the revenue control failure meets; the others are minor deficiencies.

q: Management remediates a control deficiency two months before the year end. The auditor should:
o: Conclude controls are effective as the new control now runs
Assess whether it ran long enough and weigh the earlier gap
Disregard the earlier deficiency as the opinion is as at date
Issue a disclaimer of opinion on internal financial controls
why: The IFC opinion is as at the balance sheet date but a sufficient period of operation is needed to test the new control, and the earlier failure may have caused misstatements requiring substantive work.

q: Which gives the strongest evidence of the operating effectiveness of a management review control over the expected credit loss model?
o: Inspecting the reviewer signature on the printed model output
Inquiring of the reviewer about the process actually followed
Examining criteria, thresholds and resolution of outliers
Confirming the model was run before the sign off date arrived
why: Management review controls are effective only if their precision is demonstrable, so evidence of criteria, thresholds and outlier resolution is required; a signature or inquiry does not establish precision.

q: A company outsources payroll processing to a service organisation. Under SA 402 the auditor should:
o: Understand the services and get a type 2 report before relying
Assume the controls are effective as the provider is independent
Test only the user entity controls and disregard the provider
Require the client to bring payroll processing back in house
why: SA 402 requires understanding the nature of the services and relevant controls; a type 1 report covers design and implementation only, so reliance on operating effectiveness needs a type 2 report or direct testing.
